gen_risks.description: SMEs and mid-caps face severe capacity constraints and high costs in measuring emissions, establishing MRV systems, and preparing bankable sustainability plans.
gen_risks.mitigation: Deploy Component 2 TA funds to support beneficiary enterprises in preparing Sustainability Plans, establishing MRV capacity, and conducting feasibility studies.
gen_risks.evidence: Most Mexican firms lack the capacity to measure emissions, implement energy-use... systems, and comply with reporting frameworks

gen_risks.description: PFIs have limited interest and institutional capacity to design, originate, and evaluate green loans and sustainability-linked debt instruments.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide dedicated training, guidance documents, and appraisal tools to PFI teams under Component 2 to enable product deployment.
gen_risks.evidence: Less than 15 percent of Mexican banks offer dedicated green or sustainable loan products; green lending represents less than 1 percent of their loan books.

gen_risks.description: NAFIN faces balance sheet foreign exchange risk when borrowing in foreign currencies (USD) while on-lending primarily in local currency (MXN).
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize Mexico's currency swap market to hedge FX exposure and restrict USD lending to export-oriented firms with natural hedges.
gen_risks.evidence: NAFIN will manage the FX risk on its own balance sheet using Mexico’s well developed currency swap market.

gen_risks.description: Risk of greenwashing or failure to achieve meaningful sustainability performance targets in Sustainability-Linked Loans and Green Loans.
gen_risks.mitigation: Mandate ex-ante validation and ex-post verification of Sustainability Plans and targets by qualified, independent verification entities.
gen_risks.evidence: To mitigate the risk of greenwashing, targets and results in the SP will be subject to... validation and ex-post verification by a qualified, independent validation entity.

gen_risks.description: NAFIN staff lack direct operational experience in carrying out selection and contracting processes under World Bank Procurement Regulations.
gen_risks.mitigation: Appoint a qualified internal procurement professional and receive hands-on training and close process supervision from the World Bank.
gen_risks.evidence: while NAFIN staff are familiar with the World Bank Procurement Regulations, they have not been directly involved in carrying out selection and contracting processes.

gen_risks.description: Financial management efficiency constraints and operational risks arising from reliance on legacy information systems requiring manual data consolidation.
gen_risks.mitigation: Implement strict supervisory review procedures, documented reconciliations, and targeted internal audit coverage as specified in the POM.
gen_risks.evidence: The main residual FM risks relate to efficiency constraints arising from reliance on legacy information systems requiring manual consolidation

gen_risks.description: Extreme climate weather events (heatwaves, droughts, floods) disrupt firm operations and increase loan delinquency rates among beneficiary enterprises.
gen_risks.mitigation: Channel financing towards climate-resilient and adaptation technologies while strengthening firm-level climate risk assessment capacities.
gen_risks.evidence: Extreme temperatures have been shown to raise loan delinquency rates among Mexican firms, as liquidity shortages and limited access to credit make it difficult

gen_risks.description: Women-led and women-owned businesses face persistent structural barriers and lower access to formal bank financing than male-led counterparts.
gen_risks.mitigation: Establish dedicated gender-inclusive performance targets, deploy targeted outreach campaigns, and apply Mexico's Sustainable Taxonomy Gender Equality Index.
gen_risks.evidence: women-led businesses face persistent barriers to financing: only 46 percent have ever sought credit compared to 50 percent of firms nationally

gen_risks.description: Commercial bank credit tenors (under 2 years) are too short for green technology investments requiring 5 to 10 year payback periods.
gen_risks.mitigation: Provide long-term IBRD/CCEFCF credit facilities to NAFIN and PFIs with explicit minimum maturity requirements for sub-loans.
gen_risks.evidence: SME loans are mostly provided for short-term, working-capital purposes, with the average SME loan-tenor less than two years

gen_risks.description: Implementation delays due to non-fulfillment of legal effectiveness conditions regarding adoption of the Project Operations Manual and Sustainable Finance Framework.
gen_risks.mitigation: Utilize GFPP preparation grant resources to draft and finalize the Project Operations Manual and Sustainable Finance Framework prior to effectiveness.
gen_risks.evidence: Borrower has adopted the Project Operations Manual... and the Borrower has prepared and adopted the Sustainable Finance Framework

gen_risks.description: Complex procedures, perceived transaction costs, and paperwork burden cause SMEs to drop out of sub-loan application processes.
gen_risks.mitigation: Streamline application documentation, provide direct firm-level TA support, and temporarily cover initial validation/verification costs.
gen_risks.evidence: Address lengthy procedures, limited internal SME capacity, and upfront cost hurdles as these can lead to drop-offs rather than scale.

gen_risks.description: High economy-wide fossil fuel reliance and high energy intensity expose beneficiary firms to severe energy transition risks and volatile energy prices.
gen_risks.mitigation: Require at least 50% of SLL GHG reductions to come from energy measures and allocate 40% of GL portfolio to clean energy investments.
gen_risks.evidence: This combination of fossil fuels and energy intensity means that firms are exposed to both energy-transition risks and high energy costs.

gt_risks.description: The Project channels financing to SMEs/mid-caps via NAFIN through Green Loans (GLs) and Sustainability-Linked Loans (SLLs). For GLs, E&S risk is limited (resources go to a pre-screened positive list), but SLLs operate as corporate loans, making site-specific impacts harder to trace and creating risk around traceability of environmental outcomes and possible greenwashing if sustainability targets are weak or under-monitored.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN prepared an Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) summary covering main E&S risks by key sector, disclosed at appraisal.

gt_risks.description: Introduction of new financial instruments (notably SLLs) not currently deployed in Mexico, which may lack sufficient demand, drives the technical design risk rating.
gt_risks.mitigation: Substantial TA to NAFIN, PFIs, and beneficiary enterprises (BEs) to support instrument design/deployment; GFPP grant to advance instrument design during preparation; NAFIN required to prepare and adopt a Sustainable Finance Framework (covering SLLs and GLs) acceptable to the Bank prior to effectiveness; draw on global best practices from comparable SLL facilities; Bank hands-on support during initial deployment.

gt_risks.description: The Project requires close coordination and participation of several stakeholders: different units within NAFIN, participating financial institutions (PFIs), beneficiary enterprises, and large anchor companies heading the green value chains (GVCs).
gt_risks.mitigation: Develop and deploy engagement/communication strategies pre-implementation via GFPP plus ongoing TA; establish a dedicated project implementation team within NAFIN with clear roles/responsibilities; formalize PFI participation through legal agreements defining reporting obligations and performance expectations; proactive NAFIN/WB engagement with anchor companies to encourage supplier-firm participation.

gt_risks.description: Risk that SMEs, mid-caps, and participating financial institutions may not take up the new SLL/GL products at the expected pace or scale, given evolving global sustainability policies, limited familiarity with the instruments, and possible overestimation of market demand.
gt_risks.mitigation: NAFIN business-development efforts for sustainable finance; targeted awareness and capacity-building for potential borrowers; TA to help beneficiary enterprises prepare Sustainability Plans and green investment proposals; monitor product uptake with scope to adjust instrument design/eligibility criteria, subject to Bank approval.
